clue.text: Some critic and leading light

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are taken, a run spanning the word boundaries

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of critic, all of and, and the start of leading

explanation.surface: A reviewer described as a leading light in their field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading light' reads as one phrase, but only 'light' is the definition; 'leading' is part of the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax stick with a burning wick is a simple source of illumination.

clue.text: Dispute working with French policeman in court

indicators.note: the working French policeman is placed inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
flic is French slang for a cop

explanation.surface: An argument involving a French cop who is on duty at a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A disagreement or clash between parties is a synonym for this noun.

clue.text: Similarity is doubly negative

parts.note: the phrase for resemblance is built from two negatives, a 'not' and an 'un-', that cancel out

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a classic litotes: two negative words combine to say 'rather like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is this means it resembles the other thing, an understatement expressing likeness.

clue.text: Nothing about unknown Mozart symphony

indicators.note: about signals that the word for nothing is turned round

parts.note: nil means nothing, a zero score
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: Nothing is known about some obscure Mozart symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: Mozart's Symphony No 36 is named after the Austrian city where he wrote it.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'Linz' Symphony is the nickname of Mozart's Symphony No 36, composed in that Austrian city.

clue.text: Confirm changes in dosage

indicators.note: changes tells us to rearrange the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A doctor confirms adjustments made in a patient's dosage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify an illness from its symptoms is to establish or settle what it is.

clue.text: They conquer lady's heart in short work by Keats

indicators.note: the middle of lady is placed inside the shortened phrase
short means the last letter of the phrase is cut off

parts.note: Keats wrote in verse, so his work is 'in verse'

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the word lady, whose possessive ending just links it to its heart

explanation.surface: Conquerors win a lady's heart, as in some short poem by Keats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In verse' runs together as one string before losing its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Invaders are forces who attack and overrun a territory, so they are those who conquer.

clue.text: Old minstrel, redhead, absorbs sediment

indicators.note: absorbs means the word for redhead takes the sediment inside it

parts.note: ginger is a nickname for a red-haired person
lees are the dregs that settle in wine

explanation.surface: A medieval minstrel with red hair soaks up the dregs of the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: A glee is a part-song for unaccompanied voices, popular in 18th-century England.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer of glees, old unaccompanied part-songs, was a kind of traditional singer or musician.

clue.text: Snow leopard carrying little weight

definitions.meaning: first meaning: another name for the snow leopard of Central Asia
second meaning: a small imperial unit of weight, one-sixteenth of a pound

explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' just joins the two meanings, though it suggests the leopard is laden.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a big Asian cat and an imperial measure of about 28 grams.

clue.text: Deep-seated hatred met in turbulent year

indicators.note: turbulent means stirred up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Bitter loathing encountered during a stormy year.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is lasting hostility or animosity between people.

clue.text: Boy and bird on railway

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the bird sits above the railway, so it comes first

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A boy and a chicken sitting on the train tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry is a common male first name, so it stands for a boy.

clue.text: Never ever improper by church

indicators.note: by means the church sits beside the first part

parts.note: something not acceptable is 'not on' in British idiom

explanation.surface: Something deemed never acceptable near a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' is a British idiom for unacceptable behaviour; CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Not a single time is an emphatic way of saying at no point whatever.

clue.text: Five in team going round country

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: going round suggests the letters spin into a new order

explanation.surface: Five players in a squad touring a foreign country.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnam is a nation in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Left city, rejected by wild cat

indicators.note: rejected means the city's letters are thrown back to front

parts.note: NY is New York
x stands for 'by' in dimensions and multiplication, as in 3 x 4

explanation.surface: Someone left town after being turned down by a feral cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lynx is a short-tailed feline of northern forests, a species of untamed cat.

clue.text: Many-coloured flag briefly going down

indicators.note: briefly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the yellow flag is a kind of iris
a descent is a going down

explanation.surface: A multicoloured flag being lowered quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is not a banner here but the wild iris plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridescent surfaces show shimmering rainbow hues that change with the angle of view.

parts.note: the numbers eleven to twenty each go past ten, and 1010 can be read as a clock time

explanation.walkthrough: Read 1010 as the digital time 10:10; the numbers 11 to 20 are all beyond ten.
explanation.definitionFit: On a twenty-four-hour or digital clock, 10:10 is said as this clock-time phrase.

clue.text: Made money, having added to lexicon

definitions.meaning: first meaning: minted as metal currency
second meaning: invented a new word or phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits the two senses of one past-tense verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both stamping metal currency and inventing a new expression.

clue.text: Poor rating given to a dessert

indicators.note: poor suggests the word is in bad shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A low score awarded to a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A granita is an Italian semi-frozen sweet of flavoured ice crystals.

clue.text: Time to unwind. Not half! Could be such a short break

definitions.note: the answer is a modifier describing such a break, as in a short pause

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else once rearranged
not half means one half of the word is dropped, keeping its first three letters

explanation.surface: A cheery reminder to relax, with a British 'Not half!' of agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'absolutely', but here it removes half of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause lasting a couple of minutes, like a two-minute silence, is a brief interval.

clue.text: There's a problem getting off here

definitions.text: There's a problem getting off here

parts.words: There's a problem getting off here
parts.note: getting off means dropping off to sleep, not leaving a vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like a bus or train stop, but 'getting off' means falling asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleep disorder is a condition where one cannot drop off at night.

clue.text: Any unusual touch of brown in hint of this shade?

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the word for hint

parts.note: a clue is a hint

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are arranged in an odd order
a touch is just the start, so only the first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of brown

explanation.surface: Asking whether any hint of brown spoils this colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan blue is a greenish-blue hue, a colour of the spectrum.

clue.text: Thrift as variety of spikenard. No way

indicators.note: variety suggests a different form, so the letters are rearranged
no means the letters for way are removed

parts.note: RD is road, a way

explanation.surface: Thrift sounds like a kind of spikenard, a plant with no clear path.
explanation.walkthrough: Thrift here is not frugality but a coastal plant; spikenard is an aromatic herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea pink is the common name for thrift, a pink-flowered seaside plant.

clue.text: Medicinal plant back at rear of nursery

parts.note: to back a horse is to bet on it

indicators.note: rear means the last letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of nursery

explanation.surface: A healing herb grown at the back of a garden nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' suggests behind, alongside 'rear', but it means put money on.
explanation.definitionFit: Betony is a purple-flowered herb long used in folk remedies.

clue.text: Deep-fried treats for party. Crazy!

parts.note: a do is a party
nuts means mad

explanation.surface: Someone raving about doughnuts at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: These ring-shaped sweet cakes, the American spelling of doughnuts, are fried in oil.

clue.text: Instrument from Juliet at ferry port, cycling

indicators.note: cycling means a letter moves from the front round to the back

parts.note: Oban is a Scottish west-coast ferry port
J in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A girl called Juliet plays an instrument while cycling at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Oban, in Argyll, is the main ferry terminal for the Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed musical device with a drum-like body.

clue.text: Periodic table

definitions.meaning: first meaning: happening now and then
second meaning: an ... table is a small side table

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the chemists' periodic table, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means happening at intervals, and it also names a small movable piece of furniture.

clue.text: Coming up from some barren location to town near Burnley

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top
some of the letters come from within these words

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of barren and the start of location

explanation.surface: Travelling out of a bleak spot to a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Burnley is a town in Lancashire, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Colne is a market town in Pendle, Lancashire, a few miles from Burnley.

clue.text: European Forte hotel

parts.note: f is the musical marking for forte, loud
an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: A European staying at a Forte hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Forte was a well-known British hotel group, but here it is the musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Finland is a northern European.

clue.text: Covers of Annunciation — author not known

indicators.note: the covers are the outer parts, so the whole inside of the word is stripped away, leaving two letters at each end

explanation.surface: A painting of the Annunciation whose artist is unrecorded.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon, short for anonymous, labels a work whose writer is unidentified.

clue.text: Atypical of Tacitus until a new review

indicators.note: to review is to go over again, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A critic finds something unlike Tacitus in a new study.
explanation.walkthrough: Tacitus was a Roman historian who wrote in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus wrote in Latin, so anything not in the style of Latin would be uncharacteristic of him.

clue.text: Narcissus on bedding that's timeless after First of January

indicators.note: after means the rest follows this letter

parts.note: a quilt is a bed covering

clue.text: Grand brand, yet was in trouble

indicators.note: being in trouble means things are disturbed, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A posh brand that has nonetheless hit hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In trouble' reads as one phrase, but 'in' joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Steinway is a famous manufacturer of grand pianos, a maker's name for instruments.

clue.text: Stick to suggestion of nearby containment

parts.note: in suggests being contained
here means in this nearby place

explanation.surface: A hint about something stuck close by in a container.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer split as 'in here' suggests something contained close by.
